title: graphrefly-rs: a panicking user fn corrupts wave-flags on the unwind path (source down() + receive_from_dep leave emitted_dirty/dep_batch stale; only run_wave's own node is reset by WaveGuard inside_run_wave)
trigger: RESOLVED 2026-05-29 (CSP-5 control/terminal slice, /dev-dispatch) — chose 'catch at a single wave-owner boundary and reset the touched set' (the second listed option; user-approved Phase 2). A thread-local WaveScope {owner, touched: Vec<Core>, blamed} is installed by the outermost public mutating entry (subscribe/down/up/set via with_wave_owner); the cascade runs under catch_unwind. Every node that mutates a transient wave-flag enrolls in touched (receive_from_dep / down / run_wave). On a caught panic, reset_wave_flags() restores each touched node to its between-wave baseline (inside_run_wave/emitted_dirty/emitted_tier3/pending/dep_batch/dep_dirty), leaving PERSISTED state (cache/dep_prev/dep_has_data/status/ctx.state) intact; then [[ERROR,e]] is emitted from blamed (the innermost fn that ran = a node ON the cycle, D30). The decentralized RAII alternative was rejected (can't cleanly reset dep-level dep_dirty/pending that span multiple receive calls). Teeth-verified: disabling the emitted_dirty reset makes conformance.rs::c6 fail (source drops its leading DIRTY). The WaveScope is forward-load-bearing — the same committed wave boundary batch (D12) + ctx.rewire_next deferred drain (D47) will reuse. Per-language impl (D24), no spec-amend/D#. node.rs + tests/conformance.rs::c6.

title: @graphrefly/rust dispatcher Pool::fns (Vec<NodeFn>) only pushes, never removes -- a registered fn (capturing Node/Core handles) lives for the process; deactivate/drop never frees it, so the node's NodeInner never drops. Node:Clone (CSP-5) makes capturing handles-into-fns idiomatic (C-6 does it), so the leak bites harder
trigger: RESOLUTION CHOSEN 2026-05-29 (/qa finding H, user pick = option 3): slotmap/generational pool -- handle = (slot, generation); deactivate/drop recycles the slot, invoke validates the generation. Replaces the index-as-handle_id Vec. RUST-ONLY -- TS is UNAFFECTED (TS has its own FactoryRegistry; the pool/registry is a per-language impl detail D24; conformance does not test pool internals). Sibling of B15 (TS rewire fn-swap handle GC): same problem shape, separate code -- design together for consistency, fix separately. Trigger: before CSP-2.7 higher-order operators (frequent rewire/fn-swap) ship, or if a long-running graph's pool growth is observed. Pre-existing (dispatcher predates the control/terminal slice). — DONE 2026-05-29 (/dev-dispatch, Rust-only): dispatcher.rs Pool = slotmap {slots: Vec<Slot{f:Option<NodeFn>, generation}>, free: Vec<u32>}; register reuses freed slots, unregister frees+bumps-gen+recycles, invoke validates generation (stale handle -> silent no-op, forward-safe for the future async pool's deferred callbacks). UNREGISTER TRIGGER = NodeInner::Drop (the only point a node is truly gone; deactivate can't, the node doesn't hold its fn to re-register). KEY INSIGHT: the registering node isn't pinned by the pool (the fn captures UPSTREAMS, not self), so its Drop fires and unregisters, releasing the captured Core(s). CAVEAT: a fn capturing its OWN node is a genuine Rc cycle this can't break (pool keeps it alive -> Drop never runs) -- documented as a user-level self-cycle (Weak self-handle). HANDLE WIDENED to {pool_id, handle_id, generation} (user-approved 2026-05-29): generation is a PER-LANGUAGE impl detail (D24), NOT in the protocol/IDL Handle (D7/DR-2 stays (pool_id, handle_id)) -- wire-meaningless, dropped at the wire boundary. Recorded in CLEAN-SLATE.md. b32 leak test (a fn-captured guard's Drop fires when the node drops) + 20 Rust tests + clippy + fmt green. B15 (TS sibling) still OPEN; Rust rewire fn-swap unregister lands when Rust rewire (C-8) does.
